description: Get the current status of up to 10 RFCs, Internet-Drafts, or BCP/STD/FYI series in one call. Accepts "RFC 9110", "rfc9110", "9110", draft names with or without a revision suffix ("draft-ietf-httpbis-semantics-19"), series numbers ("BCP 14"), RFC and draft file names ("rfc9110.txt"), the URL of an RFC or draft on datatracker.ietf.org, tools.ietf.org, or ietf.org or of an RFC on rfc-editor.org, and a series URL at rfc-editor.org/info/ or datatracker.ietf.org/doc/ ("https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/bcp14/"). RFCs return current and as-published status, stream, working group, obsoletes/obsoleted-by and updates/updated-by relations, the series they belong to, and the errata page; drafts return their state, IESG state, intended status, expiry, the document that replaced them, and the RFC they became; a series returns its member RFCs. Unknown ids return found: false. A call makes at most 20 Datatracker requests, retries included (an RFC or a series needs one, plus one per call for the RFCs' series; a draft three, or four with a revision suffix): each id is taken in request order if its requests still fit, and the others come back in failed with reason request_limit, to pass in another call.

ids.description: Up to 10 RFCs, Internet-Drafts, or series, e.g. ["RFC 9110", "BCP 14", "draft-ietf-httpbis-semantics-19"]. One comma-, semicolon-, or newline-separated string is also accepted.

items.description: One RFC number ("RFC 9110", "9110"), draft name, series number ("BCP 14"), RFC or draft file name, or a URL of a form the tool description lists. A URL's query and fragment are dropped before this 200-character limit applies.

name: iana_get_rfc_status

documents.description: One entry per distinct requested id, in request order, excluding ids in failed.

draft.description: Present when kind is draft and found is true.

datatracker_url.description: The draft on the IETF Datatracker.

expires.description: Expiry time of the latest revision.

requested_revision.description: The revision suffix requested, when the draft was found without it.

rfceditor_state.description: RFC Editor queue state, when in the queue.

found.description: True when the document exists upstream, or the series has member RFCs.

guidance.description: Why nothing was found and what to pass instead; on a found draft, that the requested revision does not exist.

id.description: As resolved: "RFC 9110", "BCP 14", or a draft name without revision; the id as given (a URL without its query or fragment) when unsupported, and the draft name as requested when no draft was found.

kind.description: How the id was read: an RFC, an Internet-Draft, a BCP/STD/FYI series, or unsupported text.

rfc.description: Present when kind is rfc and found is true.

datatracker_url.description: The RFC on the IETF Datatracker.

draft_name.description: The Internet-Draft it was published from.

is_also.description: The BCP, STD, or FYI series it belongs to, e.g. "BCP 14"; empty when it is in none. Absent when series membership could not be read (see notice).

published_status.description: Status at publication, which may since have changed.

status.description: Current status per the RFC Editor, e.g. "INTERNET STANDARD", "HISTORIC".

url.description: The RFC on the RFC Editor site.

series.description: Present when kind is series and found is true.

datatracker_url.description: The series on the IETF Datatracker.

members.description: Member RFCs in ascending order, e.g. "RFC 2119".

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `upstream_unreadable`: Every id failed because the RFC Editor or Datatracker sent a response that could not be read. `pacer_shed`: This server's own RFC Editor or Datatracker request queue is too full for any id to start in time. `request_limit`: An id did not fit within the call's limit of 20 Datatracker requests, a third of this server's per-minute Datatracker pacing, or retries used up the limit before it resolved. Those ids land in failed with this reason; the call itself fails with it only when no id resolved. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

failed.description: Ids whose lookup failed upstream or was cut by the call's request limit; the rest of the batch still answered.

reason.description: Failure reason, when classified: "request_limit" (call again with this id now), or an upstream one such as "upstream_unreadable".

retryable.description: Whether calling again with this id can succeed, when the failure states it: true for request_limit; false when the outcome repeats, such as an upstream redirect this server does not follow.

notice.description: Set when ids were left unresolved at the call's Datatracker request limit, or when Datatracker fields (stream and group, or series membership) were unavailable for some RFCs.

title: Get RFC, Internet-Draft, and series status
